entities.summary: Titus Menenius Lanatus was a Roman patrician and statesman who played a crucial role in shaping the early Roman Republic. Born in 550 BCE, Lanatus rose to prominence in 477 BC, when he was elected consul for the year. Despite his efforts, he was unable to prevent the disaster of the Cremera, a devastating flood that occurred in 477 BC, and was subsequently prosecuted by the tribunes of the plebs. This event marked a significant turning point in the development of the Roman Republic, as it highlighted the growing tensions between the patrician class and the plebeian masses. Lanatus's failure to prevent the disaster and his subsequent prosecution had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of Roman politics and society for generations to come. As a testament to his enduring legacy, Lanatus remains one of the most fascinating figures in Roman history, offering valuable insights into the complexities of ancient Roman politics and society.
